newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower, led by gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Thursday, led by a further slide in gold to new three year lows, on rumors of more central bank sales, but silver once more proved resilient, finding trade support late in the day, analysts said.

"The talk is there has been a central bank in the market again, after gold bounced back up to near $358 an ounce last week, with the Bank of Portugal mentioned, though that is unconfirmed," said Scott Mehlman, chief dealer with Credit Lyonnais Rouse in New York.
"The selling looked to originate in the European time zone and be led by banks and commercials rather than funds as the COMEX February/April roll is largely done now," he said.

COMEX April gold ended down $5.70 an ounce at $347.50, after seeing a new contract low at $347.30. Estimated total gold futures volume was a high 61,000 contracts, with contract lows seen in all active delivery months out to February 1998.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted at $345.35/85, a new three-year low, compared with the London Thursday afternoon fix at $349.25, and the New York close Wednesday at $351.00/50.
But short term implied lease rates rose sharply Thursday also, suggesting more speculative shorting was occurring in the bullion market, analysts said.
One month lease rates rose to around 2.04 percent from 1.72 percent Wednesday and 1.50 percent Tuesday.
Earlier, on January 13 the Dutch central bank confirmed it had sold 300 tonnes of gold in late 1996, after denying any activity on December 5.

But in mid-January, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, speaking in his capacity as chairman of the G-10 central bank governors committee, said no further G-10 central bank gold sales would occur "for the time being".

Data from the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), released Wednesday, suggesting the bullion market was larger than many anticipated, was mildly supportive though, analysts said, as it suggested the market may be able to absorb more European central bank sales than previously expected.
The LBMA reported Wednesday it cleared about 930 tonnes of gold daily in the fourth quarter 1996, worth about $10 billion a day.

Meanwhile, in data reported Thursday, COMEX gold open interest continued to decline Wednesday, suggesting commodity funds, may have been covering short positions in the past week, as well as rolling some positions into forward months, ahead of the February gold contract's first notice day Friday.
In recent months, commodity funds had been seen as the driving force behind gold's slide
Total COMEX gold open interest fell 685 lots Wednesday to 188,475 lots, and is down 16,996 contracts from 205,471 lots on January 21.
February gold open interest fell 14,176 lots to 28,620 lots Wednesday, while April open interest rose 12,921 lots to 35,698 lots.
The February/April gold spread narrowed to $1.30 an ounce Thursday, from $1.90 on Monday, as a result of the roll into forward months.
Silver remained more resilient than gold though Thursday, with the spot gold/silver ratio sliding to 70.06, from 71.19 Monday, down from a high of 80.00 last November.

COMEX March silver ended up 1.5 cents at $4.955 an ounce, after recovering late in the session, on trade buying, from a five day low at $4.860. Estimated total silver futures volume was 24,000 contracts.
Platinum was also relatively stronger than gold, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ending higher at $8.00 an ounce, from $5.60 Wednesday.
NYMEX April platinum closed down $3.40 an ounce at $355.50, after posting a new contract low at $353.90. Back months in platinum also saw new contract lows.

"The funds are still short platinum, as long as there is commercial selling in gold, but they are aware that the market is probably getting close to a bottom and stops have been tightened, so any short covering rallying could be very sharp," RJ Futures floor trader Ralph D'Esposito said.
NYMEX March palladium ended down 85 cents at $123.75.
((-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641; -email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com))
